sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author expresses or conveys (their attitude, mood, or the emotional tone of the event described). Many tweets mention dates, events, or celebrities; label by the evaluative tone, not the topic.

criteria.positive: Author shows clear enthusiasm, excitement, liking, hope, gratitude or praise, or promotes something with upbeat wording (celebrate, win, get your tickets, don't miss, please share, come support, perfect, amazing, can't wait, love, favourite, lucky, thank you, :) ). Also reported wins/achievements, condolences with prayers or blessings (RIP, may God bless), well-wishing.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports, schedules and event notices that just give logistics (register, RSVP, sign up, meeting at 6pm), spam/giveaway bait, questions, requests or pleas to celebrities, hedged opinions (may be, could be, is it still...?), live sports updates. Also light banter, wry jokes, playful hyperbole or joking self-deprecation (lol, lmao, I'm dead, not ready), mild snark, and mixed or ambivalent feelings. When the tone is joking, observational or balanced, choose neutral.
criteria.negative: Author is genuinely angry, sad, disappointed, disgusted, fearful or contemptuous (sucks, wtf, shit, hate, ugly, boring, ugh, :( ), insults or harshly mocks someone, makes pointed political/religious criticism, or wishes harm. Also reports of bad events: attacks, bombings, deaths, crimes, arrests, disputes, economic losses, scandals, injuries, product failures.
